clue.text: Start to understand wizard

parts.note: to get something is to understand it
wizard as an adjective means excellent, as does cracking

explanation.surface: Someone is told to begin grasping a sorcerer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wizard' reads as a magician but is old British slang for first-rate, like 'cracking'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to get going on a task is to begin it promptly.

clue.text: Country fair gatecrashed by United team after training

indicators.note: gatecrashed by says other pieces push their way inside the fair

parts.note: a gala is a festive fair
U is the abbreviation for United in team names

indicators.note: after training suggests the letters of team are drilled into a new shape

explanation.surface: A sports team in training barges into a fete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gatecrashed by' and 'after training' work together: the drilled team, with U before it, pushes into the fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American nation bordering Mexico.

clue.text: Bound to net everything, scored!

indicators.note: to net means to catch, so the bound word holds the other inside it

parts.note: bound means tied up
all means everything

explanation.surface: A footballer is sure to find the net with every shot and score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' is the definition in the sense of counted up.
explanation.definitionFit: To score points is to add them up, so a counted total was reckoned.

clue.text: European city, where blackguard joins female

indicators.note: joins puts the female word next to the scoundrel word

parts.note: a rotter is a scoundrel, a blackguard
a dam is a female parent animal

explanation.surface: A city where a cad hooks up with a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the great Dutch port is a city in Europe.

clue.text: Winner hard to be found in group

indicators.note: to be found in puts the hard letter inside the group word

parts.note: a camp is a faction or group
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A victor is difficult to spot among the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal short form of champion, someone who wins.

clue.text: Briefly exposing knees? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite says the phrase falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: wearing shorts leaves the knees bare

explanation.surface: Bare knees, but only nearly, in brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last S of the phrase meaning wearing shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom used to sum up concisely, meaning to put it briefly.

clue.text: Caged by ogre, beautiful bird

indicators.note: caged by says the bird sits enclosed within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A lovely bird imprisoned by a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a diving waterbird with lobed toes.

clue.text: Fight and shout about ending in uproar

indicators.note: about means going around, so the shouting word surrounds the extra letter

parts.note: to bawl is to shout loudly

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of the word uproar

explanation.surface: A scuffle breaks out with yelling as things end in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a rough, noisy scrap between people.

clue.text: We Brits also worked in domestic service

indicators.note: worked suggests the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: British people too once laboured as servants.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: servants' quarters were downstairs, so it means employed as household staff.

clue.text: Brief article is thrown back into river

indicators.note: into says the pieces go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: thrown back says the word is is read in reverse order

explanation.surface: A short item is tossed back into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown back' turns IS into SI, giving ANSI, which goes into TRENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something passing and short-lived is brief.

clue.text: Roughly nine accessing computers to see game

indicators.note: accessing means getting into, so the shuffled piece goes inside

parts.note: tablets are handheld computers

indicators.note: roughly suggests the letters of nine are roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: About nine people logging on to watch a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' scrambles nine and 'accessing' puts the result inside the handheld computers; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: ping-pong is an indoor bat-and-ball sport.

clue.text: General change brought about that flows with the wind

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general

indicators.note: brought about, like a ship turning, says the word for change is reversed

parts.note: to edit text is to change it

explanation.surface: A military leader's alteration is effected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' is a sailing term for turning a ship, here turning the word for change backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term: a current running in the same direction the wind blows.

clue.text: Saying first of prayers, itinerant heading for basilica

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of prayers
for, as in heading for, sets the wanderer going ahead of the church's letter

parts.note: an itinerant is a wanderer, a rover

indicators.note: heading means the leading letter of the word basilica

explanation.surface: A wandering pilgrim says a prayer on the way to a great church.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a short traditional maxim is a saying.

clue.text: Reportedly use woodland

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word as it is heard said, not as it is spelt

parts.note: to wield a tool is to use it

explanation.surface: Talk of putting forest land to use.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weald is a once-wooded region of south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Old word for forested country, surviving as a name in Kent and Sussex.

clue.text: Dame lacking guts, though bet she's introduced to society

indicators.note: lacking guts removes the inside letters of Dame, keeping its outer ones

parts.note: but can mean though, nevertheless
an ante is a stake put up in poker

explanation.surface: A cowardly lady places a wager anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: A young woman formally presented at court or a society ball.

clue.text: Marsupial in company with one bird

parts.note: a band is a company of people
I is the Roman numeral one
a coot is a water bird

explanation.surface: A pouched mammal keeps company with a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Australian ratlike animal that carries its young in a pouch.

clue.text: English character cut after month in story

indicators.note: after places the English character piece behind the month

parts.note: Nov is short for November

indicators.note: cut says the word for character is docked of its final letter

parts.note: a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: An English figure is removed from a tale after a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A short novel or long short story, often light.

clue.text: Business people need smart manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests moving the letters of need smart into a new order

explanation.surface: Commercial folk require clever tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopkeepers and skilled workers who trade are business people.

clue.text: School fees unlimited, old money invested

indicators.note: invested means placed inside, so the old coin goes within
unlimited strips the outer letters from fees

parts.note: a ducat was an old European gold coin

explanation.surface: Tuition charges without cap, with an old fortune put into them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is a verb here: to teach.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym of the verb: to school someone is to teach them.

clue.text: Picture instant struggle

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: A snapshot of a sudden fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A film is informally called a picture.

clue.text: I'm up pole in error

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters of I'm read bottom to top

parts.note: a stake is a pointed pole

explanation.surface: Someone stuck atop a post by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a blunder or slip is an error.

clue.text: The setter's weight is appropriate!

parts.note: the setter is I, so the setter's (setter is) gives I'm
a pound is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: The compiler claims their heaviness is fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym of the verb: to confiscate or take possession of something.

clue.text: Criticise author Eliot, rubbish!

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
T. S. Eliot, poet of The Waste Land

explanation.surface: Panning a poet's work as garbage.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: something dismissed as worthless nonsense.

clue.text: Last of spread, light as butter perhaps?

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word spread

parts.note: airy means light and insubstantial

explanation.surface: A spread finished off, light as whipped butter.
explanation.definitionFit: Butter is an example of milk produce, sold as such.

clue.text: Hormone is in lung, endlessly circulating

indicators.note: circulating suggests the letters move around into a new order
endlessly says the word lung loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A hormone moves through the lung without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts LUNG to LUN; IS, IN and LUN are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreatic hormone controlling blood sugar.

clue.text: Iran's man trembling with love for republic

indicators.note: trembling suggests the letters shake into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A nervous Iranian with his sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny independent state surrounded by Italy, one of the oldest republics.

clue.text: Drunkard reversing after gold cars

indicators.note: after places the drunkard piece behind the gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: reversing says the word for drunkard is read backwards

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A drunk backs out after a golden haul of cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns the drunkard word backwards and 'after' places it behind the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal plural for motor vehicles, chiefly American.

clue.text: Agree it's CI2I on the telephone?

indicators.note: on the telephone means heard by voice only, so the symbols are read as they sound

parts.note: the symbols are said one by one: C as see, I as eye, the digit 2 as to, I as eye

explanation.surface: Is this code what consent sounds like on a phone call?
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to share exactly the same view as someone.
